name: William Grindecobbe
role: Leader of the St Albans townsmen
description: Led the townsmen of St Albans in their long-running dispute with the town's Benedictine abbey over feudal privileges. On hearing of the London rising he traveled to the capital, obtained Wat Tyler's personal authorization for direct action against the abbey, and returned to lead the opening of the abbey prison and the burning of its manorial records in the town square on 14-16 June 1381, forcing Abbot Thomas de la Mare to grant a charter of the town's rights. Despite what he believed was a secured pardon, Grindecobbe was tried and executed at St Albans once royal authority was restored.
narrative_function: Shows the revolt's provincial-town variant -- an urban corporate grievance against a monastic lord, distinct from the rural villeinage grievance.
